category.name: SaaS applications
category.description: Incidents in business SaaS: Microsoft 365, Salesforce, Slack, GitHub, Google Workspace, file sharing, CRM, HR and data platforms, and SaaS-to-SaaS integrations.

playbooks.name: M365 mailbox compromised with a hidden forwarding or delete rule
playbooks.summary: Use when a user's Exchange Online mailbox has a new inbox rule forwarding, moving to RSS Feeds, or deleting messages, or SMTP forwarding was set, typical of business email compromise.

preparation: Confirm Unified Audit Log and MailItemsAccessed auditing are enabled for all mailboxes
Block automatic external forwarding with the outbound spam filter policy
Keep a contact path to finance for wire-fraud recall when a BEC is suspected
identification: List the user's inbox rules with Get-InboxRule -IncludeHidden and note ForwardTo, RedirectTo and DeleteMessage
Check Get-Mailbox for ForwardingSmtpAddress and DeliverToMailboxAndForward
Search UAL for New-InboxRule, Set-InboxRule and UpdateInboxRules from the user and their client IPs
Review MailItemsAccessed events to determine which messages the attacker read
Identify invoices or payment threads the attacker replied to from the mailbox
containment: Remove the malicious inbox rules and clear ForwardingSmtpAddress on the mailbox
Reset the user's password and revoke sessions with Revoke-MgUserSignInSession
Block the forwarding destination address in tenant allow/block list
eradication: Remove attacker-registered MFA methods and OAuth app consents on the account
Delete messages the attacker sent from the mailbox to internal and external recipients via Purview search
Check for mailbox delegates or SendAs permissions added during the compromise
recovery: Notify external recipients who received fraudulent payment instructions
Restore deleted messages from Recoverable Items for the user
Monitor the mailbox for rule recreation for 30 days
lessons: Alert on new inbox rules that forward externally or move to RSS Feeds or Archive
Measure whether finance verified payment changes out of band
Review how the initial credential was obtained, such as AiTM phishing

splunk.title: Inbox rule creation with forwarding or deletion
splunk.spl: index=o365 sourcetype=o365:management:activity Workload=Exchange Operation IN (New-InboxRule,Set-InboxRule,UpdateInboxRules,Set-Mailbox) | search Parameters{}.Name IN (ForwardTo,RedirectTo,ForwardAsAttachmentTo,DeleteMessage,MoveToFolder,ForwardingSmtpAddress) | table _time UserId ClientIP Operation Parameters{}.Name Parameters{}.Value

splunk.title: MailItemsAccessed by session for the compromised user
splunk.spl: index=o365 sourcetype=o365:management:activity Operation=MailItemsAccessed UserId=<suspect_user> | stats count dc(Folders{}.FolderItems{}.InternetMessageId) as messages by ClientIPAddress, SessionId, ClientInfoString | sort - messages

playbooks.name: SharePoint Online mass file download by a single account
playbooks.summary: Use when one user or app downloads or syncs hundreds of files from SharePoint sites in a short time, possibly a compromised account, departing employee, or malicious app.

preparation: Baseline per-user FileDownloaded and FileSyncDownloadedFull volumes in SharePoint
Enable Defender for Cloud Apps mass download policy for SharePoint
Apply sensitivity labels to high-value sites so impact can be scoped quickly
identification: Count FileDownloaded, FileSyncDownloadedFull and FileAccessed events per user and site
Determine whether downloads came from browser, OneDrive sync client or Graph API by UserAgent
List the sites and sensitivity labels of files downloaded
Check HR records for the user's notice period or performance actions
Correlate ClientIP with Entra sign-in logs for device compliance and location
containment: Revoke the user's sessions and block sign-in if compromise or malicious insider is suspected
Apply a Conditional Access policy restricting the user to web-only, no-download access
Remove the user from the most sensitive SharePoint site groups
eradication: Remove sync relationships for unmanaged devices from the user's account
Revoke any app registration or Graph token that performed downloads
Collect the device if it is corporate managed for forensic review
recovery: Restore normal access after investigation with legal and HR agreement
Confirm download volume returns to baseline
Provide data owners with the list of downloaded documents
lessons: Tune the mass download threshold per department
Evaluate blocking sync from unmanaged devices tenant-wide
Add departing-employee watchlist correlation to download alerts

splunk.title: Top SharePoint downloaders by file count
splunk.spl: index=o365 sourcetype=o365:management:activity Workload=SharePoint Operation IN (FileDownloaded,FileSyncDownloadedFull) | stats count dc(ObjectId) as files dc(SiteUrl) as sites values(UserAgent) as ua by UserId, ClientIP | where files>200 | sort - files

splunk.title: Download timeline for suspect user
splunk.spl: index=o365 sourcetype=o365:management:activity Workload=SharePoint Operation IN (FileDownloaded,FileSyncDownloadedFull) UserId=<suspect_user> | timechart span=15m count by SiteUrl limit=10

playbooks.name: Spike in OneDrive files shared externally or via Anyone links
playbooks.summary: Use when a user creates many external sharing invitations or Anyone links from OneDrive in a short time, a sign of exfiltration by an insider or a compromised account.

preparation: Set Anyone link expiry and default link type to Specific people in the SharePoint admin center
Restrict external sharing to allowed domains for sensitive departments
Keep a weekly baseline of external shares per user
identification: Count AnonymousLinkCreated, SharingInvitationCreated and AddedToSecureLink events per user
List recipients' external domains and check if any are personal email providers
Identify files shared and their sensitivity labels
Check AnonymousLinkUsed events to see whether links were opened and from where
containment: Remove Anyone links and external permissions on affected files with the sharing report
Temporarily disable external sharing for the user's OneDrive
Suspend the account if sharing is not explained by the user
eradication: Revoke guest accounts created by the user's invitations if not legitimate
Remove sync to personal devices
Reset credentials if the account was compromised
recovery: Re-share legitimately needed files with Specific people links
Confirm external sharing counts return to normal
Inform data owners of accessed links
lessons: Alert when a user creates more than N Anyone links in an hour
Review DLP policy coverage for OneDrive sharing
Consider making Anyone links unavailable for labeled content

splunk.title: External shares and Anyone links per user
splunk.spl: index=o365 sourcetype=o365:management:activity Workload=OneDrive Operation IN (AnonymousLinkCreated,SharingInvitationCreated,AddedToSecureLink,CompanyLinkCreated) | stats count dc(ObjectId) as files values(TargetUserOrGroupName) as recipients by UserId, Operation | sort - files

splunk.title: Anyone link usage from outside
splunk.spl: index=o365 sourcetype=o365:management:activity Operation=AnonymousLinkUsed SiteUrl="*<suspect_user_slug>*" | stats count by ClientIP, ObjectId

playbooks.name: Teams external access used for phishing or malware delivery
playbooks.summary: Use when external tenants message employees in Microsoft Teams posing as IT or helpdesk, sending links or files, or initiating remote support sessions.

preparation: Configure Teams external access to an allow list of partner domains
Enable Teams message auditing and Safe Links for Teams
Brief the helpdesk on how it will and will not contact users through Teams
identification: Search UAL for ChatCreated and MessageSent where the sender tenant is external
Identify the external tenant ID and display names used, such as Help Desk
List every internal user who accepted the chat or replied
Check endpoints of contacted users for Quick Assist, AnyDesk or other remote tool launches
Review URLs and files shared in the chat with Defender for Office 365
containment: Block the external domain in Teams external access settings
Isolate endpoints where remote tools were launched after the chat
Reset credentials of users who shared codes or passwords in the chat
eradication: Uninstall remote access tools installed during the session
Remove malicious files from Teams and SharePoint via Purview content search
Hunt for persistence on endpoints touched by the remote session
recovery: Notify all employees of the pretext with screenshots
Confirm the blocked tenant cannot initiate chats
Re-enable affected users after endpoint remediation
lessons: Detect external chats whose display name contains help, support or IT
Consider disabling chat with unmanaged Teams accounts
Track how many users engaged before the block

splunk.title: External Teams chats to internal users
splunk.spl: index=o365 sourcetype=o365:management:activity Workload=MicrosoftTeams Operation IN (ChatCreated,MessageSent) ParticipantInfo.HasForeignTenantUsers=true | stats count dc(UserId) as recipients values(UserId) as users by ParticipantInfo.ParticipatingTenantIds{}, ChatName

splunk.title: Remote support tools started after the chat
splunk.spl: | tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as first from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("QuickAssist.exe","AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(first)

playbooks.name: Salesforce bulk data export or report exfiltration
playbooks.summary: Use when Salesforce event logs show large report exports, Bulk API queries, or Data Export jobs by an unusual user or from a new IP, indicating CRM data theft.

preparation: License Salesforce Shield Event Monitoring and ingest ReportExport, BulkApi and API events
Restrict Export Reports and Weekly Data Export permissions to named profiles
Enable Transaction Security policies for large report exports
identification: Query ReportExport events for row counts and report names by user
Review BulkApi and API events for SOQL queries against Contact, Account and Opportunity
Check Setup Audit Trail for Data Export Service schedules created by the user
Compare the session's SOURCE_IP and USER_AGENT to the user's normal login history
Identify whether access came through a connected app or direct login
containment: Freeze the user in Setup and end their active sessions
Remove Export Reports and API Enabled permissions from the user's permission set
Add the source IP to a login IP restriction denial or restrict trusted IP ranges on the profile
eradication: Cancel scheduled data exports and delete pending export files
Reset the password and security token for the account
Revoke OAuth tokens for connected apps the user authorized
recovery: Restore permissions after review with least privilege
Confirm no further large exports occur
Give legal the object types and record counts exported
lessons: Add an alert for ReportExport events above a row threshold
Review how many users hold Export Reports and reduce it
Assess whether Transaction Security could have blocked the export in real time

splunk.title: Large report exports by user
splunk.spl: index=salesforce sourcetype=sfdc:logfile EVENT_TYPE=ReportExport | stats count sum(ROW_COUNT) as rows values(REPORT_ID_DERIVED) as reports by USER_ID_DERIVED, CLIENT_IP | sort - rows

splunk.title: Bulk API and API queries by user
splunk.spl: index=salesforce sourcetype=sfdc:logfile EVENT_TYPE IN (BulkApi,API,RestApi) USER_ID_DERIVED=<suspect_user> | stats count sum(ROWS_PROCESSED) as rows by ENTITY_NAME, CLIENT_IP, USER_AGENT | sort - rows

splunk.title: Setup Audit Trail data export scheduling
splunk.spl: index=salesforce sourcetype=sfdc:setupaudittrail Section="Data Export" | table _time CreatedByUsername Action Display

playbooks.name: Malicious or compromised Salesforce connected app accessing org data
playbooks.summary: Use when a new connected app is authorized in Salesforce, or an existing integration's OAuth tokens are used from unknown IPs to pull records via API, including vishing-led Data Loader installs.

preparation: Set connected apps to Admin approved users are pre-authorized and block uninstalled app use
Keep an inventory of approved connected apps with owners and IP ranges
Ingest LoginHistory and ConnectedAppPlugin and API events into the SIEM
identification: List connected apps and OAuth usage in Setup and find apps installed or first used recently
Review LoginHistory for OAuth logins by the app and their source IPs
Check whether a user was talked into authorizing a Data Loader style app over the phone
Count records queried by the app's sessions in API events
Identify the authorizing users and their profiles
containment: Revoke all OAuth tokens for the app in Connected Apps OAuth Usage
Block the connected app or set its policy to admin-approved only with no users assigned
Restrict the app's IP relaxation to enforce trusted ranges
eradication: Uninstall the unauthorized connected app
Rotate the consumer secret for legitimate apps whose tokens leaked
Reset credentials for users who authorized the app under social engineering
recovery: Re-authorize legitimate integrations with new credentials
Confirm API usage by the app has stopped
Notify affected customers if exfiltrated records include personal data
lessons: Alert on first-seen connected app OAuth logins
Train support and sales staff on vishing pretexts that request app authorization
Require API Enabled permission only for integration users

splunk.title: OAuth logins by connected app and IP
splunk.spl: index=salesforce sourcetype=sfdc:loginhistory LoginType="Remote Access 2.0" | stats count min(_time) as first dc(UserId) as users by Application, SourceIp | convert ctime(first) | sort first

splunk.title: API row volume by connected app
splunk.spl: index=salesforce sourcetype=sfdc:logfile EVENT_TYPE IN (API,RestApi,BulkApi) CONNECTED_APP_ID=<app_id> | stats sum(ROWS_PROCESSED) as rows count by ENTITY_NAME, CLIENT_IP | sort - rows

playbooks.name: Slack bot or user token leaked and used to read channels
playbooks.summary: Use when a Slack xoxb, xoxp or xoxc token is found in code, logs or a public paste, or the Slack audit log shows a token reading many channels or files from an unfamiliar IP.

preparation: Ingest Slack audit logs (Enterprise Grid) and Access Logs into the SIEM
Enable token rotation for Slack apps and restrict app installs to admin approval
Add Slack token patterns to source code secret scanning
identification: Determine the token type and owner (bot, user, or session cookie) and the app it belongs to
Review the app's OAuth scopes such as channels:history, files:read and users:read.email
Search audit logs for actions by the token's user or app from new IPs
Identify channels and files accessed and whether private channels or DMs were in scope
Find where and when the token was exposed
containment: Revoke the token with auth.revoke or by reinstalling the app
Sign the user out of all sessions in the admin console if a user token or cookie leaked
Restrict the app to specific channels until reissued
eradication: Remove the token from the repo history and CI logs
Rotate the app's signing secret and client secret
Scan channels the token could read for secrets pasted by users and rotate them
recovery: Reissue a new token with minimal scopes and store it in a secrets manager
Confirm audit logs show no use of the old token
Notify channel owners of the exposure where sensitive content was readable
lessons: Enforce IP allow lists for Slack app tokens where supported
Reduce bot scopes that grant history across all channels
Track time from token exposure to revocation

splunk.title: Slack audit actions by app or user from new IPs
splunk.spl: index=slack sourcetype=slack:audit (actor.user.id=<suspect_user> OR entity.app.id=<app_id>) | stats count values(action) as actions min(_time) as first by context.ip_address, context.ua | convert ctime(first)

splunk.title: File downloads and channel history reads
splunk.spl: index=slack sourcetype=slack:audit action IN (file_downloaded,file_downloaded_blocked,file_public_link_created) | stats count by actor.user.name, context.ip_address, action | sort - count

playbooks.name: Slack workspace or organization data export initiated
playbooks.summary: Use when an admin or owner starts a full workspace export, a corporate export including DMs, or a discovery API pull that was not requested by legal or compliance.

preparation: Limit Slack Owner and Admin roles and record who is allowed to run exports
Route export notifications to the security mailbox as well as owners
Document the legal and compliance process for legitimate exports
identification: Find export_started, corporate_exports_approved and export_downloaded events in the audit log
Confirm with legal whether a matter or request exists for the export
Identify the export scope: public channels only, or all channels and DMs
Check the downloading IP and device against the admin's normal access
containment: Cancel the export if still running and expire the download link
Demote the admin and reset their credentials if the export is unauthorized
Sign out the account from all devices
eradication: Audit other admin actions by the account such as SSO or retention changes
Remove additional admins the account promoted
Revoke Discovery API tokens or apps the admin authorized
recovery: Restore admin roster to the approved list
Notify affected staff or regulators as legal directs
Re-verify export settings and approvals
lessons: Alert on any export_started event in real time
Require two-person approval for corporate exports
Review whether retention settings reduce exposure of old DMs

splunk.title: Slack export events
splunk.spl: index=slack sourcetype=slack:audit action IN (export_started,export_completed,export_downloaded,corporate_exports_approved,corporate_exports_enabled) | table _time actor.user.email action context.ip_address entity.workspace.name details.export_type

splunk.title: Other admin actions by the exporting account
splunk.spl: index=slack sourcetype=slack:audit actor.user.email=<suspect_user> earliest=-30d | stats count by action | sort - count

playbooks.name: GitHub organization admin compromise or repo visibility changes
playbooks.summary: Use when a GitHub org owner account adds members, changes repository visibility to public, disables branch protection, or alters org security settings without a change request.

preparation: Stream the GitHub Enterprise audit log to the SIEM including Git events
Require SSO and two-factor for all org members and keep owner count minimal
Disable members' ability to change repository visibility in org settings
identification: Search the audit log for repo.access, org.add_member, org.update_member and protected_branch.destroy
List repositories whose visibility changed to public and the exact time
Check org.disable_two_factor_requirement and SSO configuration changes
Identify new deploy keys, outside collaborators, and GitHub Apps installed
Review the owner's actor_ip and user agent against normal behavior
containment: Revert public repositories to private immediately
Remove the compromised owner's org role and revoke their SSO sessions and PATs
Remove outside collaborators and deploy keys added during the window
eradication: Restore branch protection and rulesets from your baseline configuration
Uninstall unauthorized GitHub Apps and revoke OAuth apps the owner approved
Rotate secrets that appear in repositories that were public, even briefly
recovery: Request removal of forks and cached copies through GitHub support where possible
Re-enable two-factor and SSO requirements and confirm member compliance
Re-establish owner accounts with hardware security keys
lessons: Alert on repo.access events that set visibility to public
Track how long sensitive code was exposed and how many clones occurred
Review break-glass owner account protections

splunk.title: Repository visibility and protection changes
splunk.spl: index=github sourcetype=github:audit action IN (repo.access,protected_branch.destroy,protected_branch.update_admin_enforced,repository_ruleset.destroy) | table _time actor actor_ip action repo visibility

splunk.title: Membership and org security setting changes
splunk.spl: index=github sourcetype=github:audit action IN (org.add_member,org.update_member,org.add_outside_collaborator,org.disable_two_factor_requirement,org.sso_response,public_key.create,integration_installation.create) | stats count values(action) as actions by actor, actor_ip

splunk.title: Clones of repositories while public
splunk.spl: index=github sourcetype=github:audit action=git.clone repo=<repo> | stats count by actor_ip, actor, repository_public

playbooks.name: Google Drive files shared publicly or to anyone with the link
playbooks.summary: Use when Google Workspace Drive audit shows files changed to public on the web or anyone with the link, especially sensitive folders or bulk changes by one user.

preparation: Set Drive sharing defaults to restrict link sharing outside the domain for sensitive OUs
Ingest Drive audit logs via the Reports API
Enable Workspace DLP rules for regulated data in Drive
identification: Search Drive events for change_document_visibility to people_with_link or public_on_the_web
List the affected doc titles, owners and their visibility before and after
Check view events from external or anonymous viewers on the exposed files
Determine whether the change was intentional publishing or a compromised account
containment: Revert the files to restricted visibility using the security investigation tool bulk action
Disable link sharing outside the domain for the user's OU temporarily
Suspend the account if the sharing is unauthorized
eradication: Remove external collaborators added at the same time
Check Apps Script projects owned by the user for automated sharing
Reset the user's password and sign-in cookies if compromised
recovery: Request removal of any search engine cache of public documents
Confirm no public files remain via a Drive inventory query
Inform data owners of the exposure window
lessons: Alert on public_on_the_web visibility for files with DLP labels
Review OUs that still allow public sharing
Measure count of documents exposed and duration

splunk.title: Drive visibility changes to public or link
splunk.spl: index=gws sourcetype=gws:reports:drive event.name=change_document_visibility (event.parameters.visibility=people_with_link OR event.parameters.visibility=public_on_the_web) | table _time actor.email event.parameters.doc_title event.parameters.owner event.parameters.old_visibility event.parameters.visibility

splunk.title: Anonymous or external views of exposed files
splunk.spl: index=gws sourcetype=gws:reports:drive event.name=view event.parameters.doc_id=<doc_id> | stats count by actor.email, ipAddress

playbooks.name: Box or Dropbox mass sharing or download by one account
playbooks.summary: Use when Box or Dropbox Business logs show one user creating many shared links, adding external collaborators, or downloading large folder trees, suggesting exfiltration.

preparation: Ingest Box admin events and Dropbox team events into the SIEM
Set shared link defaults to company-only and require expiry for open links
Classify top-level folders with Box Shield or Dropbox labels
identification: Count SHARE, COLLABORATION_INVITE and DOWNLOAD events per user in Box admin logs
Count shared_link_create and file_download events per member in Dropbox team events
Identify external collaborator domains and link access levels
Determine data classification of the folders involved
Check whether the activity used the desktop client, web or an API app
containment: Disable shared links and remove external collaborators on affected folders
Suspend the user or revoke their active sessions and linked devices
Revoke API app authorizations the user granted
eradication: Remove the content from the user's personal space if it was copied there
Reset the account credentials and reenroll MFA
Remote wipe Box Drive or Dropbox desktop caches on unmanaged devices
recovery: Restore collaborations needed for business with expiring links
Confirm event volume returns to baseline
Give legal the folder list and external parties
lessons: Add Box Shield or Dropbox anomaly alerts to SOC routing
Review whether open links should be disallowed for classified folders
Track mean time to revoke links

splunk.title: Box sharing and download volume per user
splunk.spl: index=box sourcetype=box:events event_type IN (SHARE,COLLABORATION_INVITE,DOWNLOAD,ITEM_SHARED_CREATE) | stats count by created_by.login, event_type | sort - count

splunk.title: Dropbox shared links and downloads per member
splunk.spl: index=dropbox sourcetype=dropbox:team:events event_type.tag IN (shared_link_create,file_download,shared_content_add_member) | stats count by actor.user.email, event_type.tag, origin.geo_location.ip_address | sort - count

playbooks.name: Zoom meeting bombing or cloud recording exposure
playbooks.summary: Use when uninvited participants disrupt Zoom meetings, meeting links leak publicly, or cloud recordings are shared without passcodes or downloaded by outsiders.

preparation: Enforce waiting rooms, passcodes and authenticated users for internal meetings by account setting lock
Require passcodes and expiry on shared cloud recordings
Ingest Zoom operation logs and webhooks into the SIEM
identification: Pull the meeting participant report for joiner names, emails and IPs
Determine where the meeting link was posted, such as a public calendar or social site
Review recording share settings and download events for affected recordings
Check operation logs for setting changes that disabled waiting rooms or passcodes
containment: End the meeting and regenerate the meeting ID and passcode
Disable share links for the exposed recordings
Lock the account setting that was changed at the account level
eradication: Delete or restrict recordings that contain sensitive content
Remove public posts of the meeting link where controllable
Report abusive participants to Zoom trust and safety
recovery: Reschedule the meeting with registration and authentication required
Confirm recordings now require sign-in to view
Communicate meeting hygiene guidance to the host's team
lessons: Audit large recurring meetings that use static links
Track recordings shared publicly per quarter
Decide whether external recording sharing should be disabled by default

splunk.title: Zoom setting changes weakening meeting security
splunk.spl: index=zoom sourcetype=zoom:operationlogs category_type IN ("Account","User Settings") (action="*Waiting Room*" OR action="*Passcode*" OR operation_detail="*passcode*") | table _time operator category_type action operation_detail

splunk.title: Recording downloads and shares
splunk.spl: index=zoom sourcetype=zoom:webhook event IN (recording.downloaded,recording.shared,recording.completed) payload.object.topic="<meeting_topic>" | table _time event payload.operator payload.object.share_url

playbooks.name: Confluence spaces scraped by an account or API token
playbooks.summary: Use when Atlassian access logs show an account or API token viewing or exporting thousands of Confluence pages across spaces, a common pre-extortion data theft pattern.

preparation: Enable Atlassian Guard user activity logs and send audit logs to the SIEM
Restrict API token creation via Atlassian Admin policy for managed accounts
Mark spaces containing credentials or architecture docs as restricted
identification: Count page views and exports per account across spaces in the activity log
Check for space export or PDF export events and API calls to /wiki/rest/api/content
Identify the API token used and when it was created
List spaces accessed and search their content for credentials or keys
Compare IP and user agent with the account's normal pattern
containment: Revoke the account's API tokens from Atlassian Admin
Suspend the account and log out its sessions
Restrict the most sensitive spaces to a smaller group
eradication: Rotate any secrets found in pages the account viewed
Remove pages that hold plaintext credentials and move them to a vault
Reset the account's identity provider credentials
recovery: Restore access after validation
Confirm activity log shows normal page view volume
Inform space owners of what was read
lessons: Alert when an account views more than N distinct pages in an hour
Scan Confluence regularly for secrets
Review API token policy exceptions

splunk.title: Confluence page views per account
splunk.spl: index=atlassian sourcetype=atlassian:confluence:audit (action="page_viewed" OR action="space_exported" OR action="page_exported") | stats count dc(attributes.container_id) as spaces by actor.email, location.ip | sort - count

splunk.title: API token creation and use
splunk.spl: index=atlassian sourcetype=atlassian:org:audit action IN (api_token_created,api_token_used) actor.email=<suspect_user> | table _time action location.ip attributes.token_label

playbooks.name: Jira or Confluence site admin account compromised
playbooks.summary: Use when an Atlassian org or site admin changes SSO, adds admins, installs Marketplace apps, or modifies global permissions unexpectedly.

preparation: Limit org admins and enforce SSO with phishing-resistant MFA for them
Stream Atlassian organization audit logs to the SIEM
Restrict Marketplace app installs to admin request workflow
identification: Review org audit for admin role grants, identity provider changes and domain verification
List Marketplace or Forge apps installed recently and their scopes
Check Jira global permissions and Confluence global permission changes
Identify new user API tokens or service accounts created by the admin
containment: Remove admin rights from the compromised account and revoke sessions
Revert SAML or identity provider configuration to the approved settings
Uninstall apps installed during the incident
eradication: Remove admins and accounts the attacker added
Revoke API tokens and OAuth integrations they created
Reset the admin's identity provider credentials and MFA
recovery: Restore global permissions from documented baseline
Confirm SSO enforcement is active for all managed accounts
Verify no further admin changes from unknown actors
lessons: Alert on identity provider or admin role changes in the Atlassian org
Keep a configuration export to compare against after incidents
Review whether admin accounts are separate from daily-use accounts

splunk.title: Atlassian org admin and SSO changes
splunk.spl: index=atlassian sourcetype=atlassian:org:audit action IN (user_granted_role,org_admin_added,saml_config_updated,identity_provider_updated,domain_verified,app_installed) | table _time actor.email action location.ip context

splunk.title: Jira global permission changes
splunk.spl: index=atlassian sourcetype=atlassian:jira:audit category=permissions | stats count values(summary) as changes by authorAccountId, remoteAddress

playbooks.name: ServiceNow instance data exposed via public widget or ACL misconfiguration
playbooks.summary: Use when ServiceNow knowledge bases, Service Portal widgets or tables are readable by unauthenticated users, or a guest session queries records via REST or the Table API.

preparation: Apply the ServiceNow security baseline for ACLs and Service Portal public widgets
Send syslog transactions and sys_audit to the SIEM
Keep a list of knowledge bases intended for public access
identification: Query transaction logs for requests by the guest user to /api/now/table and widget endpoints
Review ACLs on sensitive tables such as sys_user, incident and kb_knowledge for public role
Check Service Portal widgets marked public that return record data
Identify records returned to unauthenticated sessions and their content
containment: Remove the public role from affected ACLs and widgets
Set the glide.security.use_csrf_token and public page restrictions per baseline
Block source IPs that bulk-queried the instance
eradication: Rotate credentials or secrets stored in exposed records
Review user criteria on knowledge bases for public exposure
Remove unused public pages and widgets
recovery: Re-test public pages with an unauthenticated session
Confirm guest transactions no longer return data
Notify data owners of exposed record types
lessons: Add a scheduled scan for public ACLs on sensitive tables
Alert on high-volume guest transactions
Include ServiceNow ACL review in each upgrade cycle

splunk.title: Unauthenticated Table API and widget requests
splunk.spl: index=servicenow sourcetype=snow:syslog_transaction user=guest (url="*/api/now/table/*" OR url="*/api/now/sp/widget/*") | stats count by url, client_ip | sort - count

splunk.title: ACL changes on sensitive tables
splunk.spl: index=servicenow sourcetype=snow:sys_audit tablename=sys_security_acl | table _time user documentkey fieldname oldvalue newvalue

playbooks.name: Workday direct deposit or payroll change by compromised account
playbooks.summary: Use when an employee reports missing pay, or Workday shows bank account changes made from unusual IPs or right after a password reset, indicating payroll diversion fraud.

preparation: Require step-up MFA in Workday for payment election changes
Notify employees by a separate channel when banking details change
Ingest Workday sign-on and business process audit reports into the SIEM
identification: Pull the Change Payment Elections business process history for affected workers
Compare sign-on IPs and user agents for the change against the worker's history
Search for multiple workers whose payment elections changed to the same bank routing number
Check identity provider logs for MFA resets or help desk password resets before the change
containment: Revert payment elections and hold the next payroll run for affected workers
Reset passwords and revoke sessions for affected accounts

playbooks.name: HubSpot or CRM contact database exported by unusual user
playbooks.summary: Use when a marketing or sales CRM such as HubSpot shows a full contacts or companies export, or a private app token pulling records, by a user or integration not normally doing so.

preparation: Restrict the Export permission in HubSpot to a named group of super admins
Enable export notifications to the security mailbox
Ingest HubSpot account audit logs and login history

Check the user's login history for IP and country changes
Identify private app or API key usage pulling contacts via the CRM API
Confirm with the user's manager whether the export was business-justified
containment: Remove export permission from the user and deactivate the account if unexplained
Rotate private app access tokens used for the pull
Revoke connected app integrations installed recently
eradication: Delete copies of the export from shared drives the user can access
Reset credentials and force MFA enrollment
Remove the user's API keys and personal access keys
recovery: Restore least-privilege permission sets for the team
Confirm no repeat exports
Assess privacy notification requirements for exported contacts
lessons: Alert on any export above a contact count threshold
Add departing-employee checks to CRM export alerts
Review how many users can export

playbooks.name: Zendesk support agent account taken over to access customer data
playbooks.summary: Use when a Zendesk agent or admin logs in from an unusual location, views or exports many tickets, changes customer emails, or creates API tokens, often used for social engineering of customers.

preparation: Enforce SSO for Zendesk agents and disable native password login
Ingest Zendesk audit logs and access logs into the SIEM
Restrict API token creation to admins
identification: Pull the agent's access log for IPs and the audit log for ticket views and exports
Look for changes to end-user email or phone that enable customer account takeover
Check for new API tokens, OAuth clients or webhook targets
List customers whose tickets were viewed in the window
containment: Suspend the agent and revoke their sessions in Zendesk and the identity provider
Revoke API tokens and OAuth clients created during the window
Revert end-user contact changes made by the agent
eradication: Delete webhooks and triggers that forward ticket content externally
Reset the agent's identity provider credentials
Review macros the attacker modified to include phishing links
recovery: Contact customers whose accounts were changed to confirm control
Restore the agent after training and credential reset
Monitor for repeat logins from the attacker IPs
lessons: Alert on end-user identity changes by agents followed by password resets
Limit agent ability to change verified customer email
Measure customers affected

playbooks.name: DocuSign account abused to send phishing or fraudulent envelopes
playbooks.summary: Use when a compromised DocuSign user sends envelopes with lookalike invoices, payment change requests or credential-harvest links from your legitimate account to customers or vendors.

preparation: Federate DocuSign to your identity provider with MFA
Enable DocuSign Monitor and ingest its events
Restrict who can create templates and bulk send

Check for new templates, brand changes or bulk send lists
Review login events for IP, location and authentication method
Extract URLs inside sent documents and check them in the sandbox

Close the user's sessions and disable the DocuSign user
Block the phishing URLs at the proxy and mail gateway
eradication: Delete attacker templates and bulk send lists
Reset the user's identity provider credentials and MFA
Remove API integration keys created by the user
recovery: Notify recipients that envelopes were fraudulent and what to do
Re-enable the user after verification
Confirm no new envelopes from the attacker sessions
lessons: Alert on bulk sends to external recipients from non-sales users
Track recipients who signed or clicked
Review whether vendor payment changes accept DocuSign as verification

playbooks.name: Snowflake account accessed with stolen credentials and data staged out
playbooks.summary: Use when Snowflake login history shows password-only logins from new IPs or clients, followed by SHOW TABLES, large SELECTs, COPY INTO an external stage or GET commands.

preparation: Enforce MFA or key-pair auth for all Snowflake users and block password-only service users
Apply network policies restricting login to corporate and integration IPs
Ingest LOGIN_HISTORY, QUERY_HISTORY and ACCESS_HISTORY from SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE
identification: Query LOGIN_HISTORY for successful password logins with FIRST_AUTHENTICATION_FACTOR=PASSWORD from new IPs

Search QUERY_HISTORY for SHOW TABLES, COPY INTO @stage, CREATE STAGE and GET by the session
Use ACCESS_HISTORY to list base objects and columns read
Identify the infostealer-infected host where the credential was captured if known
containment: Disable the user with ALTER USER SET DISABLED = TRUE and abort its running queries
Apply an account-level network policy blocking the attacker IPs
Drop external stages and storage integrations the attacker created
eradication: Rotate passwords and keys for every user that logged in from the attacker IPs
Remove roles granted to the compromised user during the session
Reimage the device that leaked the credential
recovery: Re-enable users with MFA or key-pair only
Confirm no logins from attacker infrastructure after containment
Provide legal with tables, row counts and data types exfiltrated
lessons: Make password-only authentication impossible by authentication policy
Alert on COPY INTO external stages not owned by data engineering
Track credentials discovered in infostealer logs as a preventive feed

playbooks.name: Notion workspace page published to the web with internal data
playbooks.summary: Use when an internal Notion page or database is shared to the web, indexed by search engines, or allows duplication, exposing roadmaps, credentials, customer lists or HR notes.

preparation: Disable Share to web for members on the Enterprise plan or restrict to workspace owners
Ingest Notion audit log events into the SIEM
Tell teams where public content should be published instead

Identify secrets or personal data in the exposed pages and child databases

Disable search engine indexing and duplication on any page that must stay public
Remove guest access that was granted at the same time
eradication: Rotate any credentials or API keys visible on the page
Request search engine removal of cached copies
Move sensitive content to a restricted teamspace
recovery: Republish only approved content in a dedicated public teamspace
Confirm the URL now returns an access request page
Notify owners of exposed personal data
lessons: Alert on every share-to-web event outside marketing teamspaces
Run periodic scans for public notion.site pages tied to your workspace
Measure the time the page was public

playbooks.name: Third-party SaaS vendor notifies you of a breach affecting your tenant
playbooks.summary: Use when a SaaS provider reports a breach, stolen support credentials, or compromised integration that may expose your data or tokens, and you must scope impact without full logs.

preparation: Maintain a SaaS inventory listing data types, integrations, tokens and admin contacts per vendor
Ensure contracts require breach notification with indicators and timelines
Store vendor log export instructions and support escalation contacts

Identify downstream systems the vendor integration could reach

Revoke and reissue OAuth grants the vendor app holds in your identity provider
Restrict the vendor integration to read-only or disable it until the vendor confirms remediation
eradication: Remove stale integrations and unused service accounts tied to the vendor
Reset passwords for any local accounts on the vendor platform
Request vendor confirmation of the root cause fix and token invalidation
recovery: Re-enable the integration with new credentials and narrowed scopes
Assess whether customer or employee notification is required based on data types
Track vendor follow-up reports until closure

Revisit the vendor's risk tier and contract terms

playbooks.name: Unsanctioned SaaS app discovered holding company data
